guarantees.claim: For each share i (0 to Share-1), msg_data_masked[i] is continuously assigned as the bitwise XOR of msg_data[i] with the AND of a MsgWidth-bit replication of cfg_msg_mask and static_mask.

assumptions.claim: static_mask and cfg_msg_mask must be configured so that msg_data_masked[i] effectively masks the secret bits of msg_data[i]; in particular, static_mask should not zero out mask bits covering sensitive data.
assumptions.risk: If static_mask has zeros over secret-bit positions or cfg_msg_mask is constant zero, msg_data_masked[i] equals msg_data[i] unmasked, exposing side‑channel leakage.

assumptions.claim: Parameter MsgWidth must match the bit width of msg_data[i] and msg_data_masked[i] to avoid width mismatch and ensure the masking applies to all bits.
assumptions.risk: A width mismatch can cause synthesis warnings or leave bits unmasked due to truncation/extension.

uncertain_points.claim: The constant static_mask may contain zeros that inhibit masking of some bits, possibly including secret key/data bits, under the described 'optimized masking scheme'.
uncertain_points.cond: if static_mask has any zero bit that corresponds to a secret data bit
uncertain_points.risk: Secret key or intermediate data appears unmasked in msg_data_masked, enabling power/EM side‑channel attacks.
